title: Workflow Entity
description: JSON Schema for the root workflow entity in customer workspace. A workflow is a flow. Flow nodes (connection, transformation, validation, data product) reference the workflow via workflow_id and point upstream via upstream_entity_id; the workflow does not store node IDs. template_id identifies the flow starter template used to create this flow (e.g. blank, webhook-ingestion), distinct from connector catalog templates.

template_id.description: Workflow starter template identifier used when this flow was created (e.g. blank, webhook-ingestion). Distinct from connector catalog templates.

workflow_type.description: Type of flow: ingestion (ingest from external sources), enrichment (transform/join data), delivery (expose or deliver data products to external systems).

segments.description: Visual groupings of nodes in the graph editor.

node_ids.description: Entity IDs of nodes in this segment

trigger.description: Workflow trigger configuration (event, schedule, or connector).

schedule.description: Cron or interval for scheduled execution

query_trigger.description: D14 (docs/system-spec/11-delivery-layer-design.md): a saved query against a data product, run on a schedule or on demand, targeting a data-products node (materialize) or an outbound connections node (deliver) chosen separately at build time. Not a subsystem — a trigger type, like event/schedule/connector above.

data_product_id.description: An existing data product — never a raw table.

query.description: The saved SQL query run against data_product_id.

schedule.description: Cron or interval; omit for on-demand (run_trigger / MCP-invoked).

primary_key.description: Source columns concatenated into lx__id before queue write (business identity).

configuration.description: Workflow configuration (schedule, batch_size, etc.). Flow nodes are discovered by workflow_id and upstream_entity_id; the workflow does not store connection_id or transformation_ids.

batch_size.description: Number of events to process per batch

activation.description: Explicit activation designation for a delivery flow's head (D7, docs/system-spec/11-delivery-layer-design.md). 'request' marks a consumer-initiated delivery flow: no schedule, no event subscription — the flow is activated by an inbound request against a protocol-adapter registration (route/listener + policy binding) rather than a queue-consumer bot. Distinguishes a deliberately request-activated flow from one whose trigger was simply never configured.

data_product_id.description: Data product this delivery flow serves. Required in practice when activation is 'request' (protocol-adapter registration) or when a schedule is set (scheduled consumption). Optional at schema level so existing schedule-free event/queue flows remain valid.

connector_type.description: Protocol/connector type for a request-activated delivery flow (e.g. sql-query). Codegen falls back to 'unknown' when omitted.

deployment.description: Deployment information (set when workflow is deployed)

metrics.description: Workflow metrics (events processed, error rate, etc.)

created_by.description: User ID who created the workflow

updated_by.description: User ID who last updated the workflow

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when workflow was created

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when workflow was last updated

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when workflow was deleted (soft delete)

archived_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when workflow was archived (catalog preserved, runtime bots retired)
